context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Replace the denylist with an explicit allow-list. The current `exclude: ['password', 'totpSecret']` is fragile: any sensitive or unneeded field added to UserModel later (reset tokens, session IDs, internal flags, nested relations) is exposed by default. Define a User response shape that lists only the fields each response needs, for example `{ id, name }` for public or peer views and a broader set for the record owner or an authorised admin. Build it with a single shared serializer or projection (e.g., a Mongoose `select` allow-list or a DTO/`toJSON` mapper) so the limits are enforced in one place. Do not return whole UserModel documents or populated nested records; project any related records to their own allow-lists. Apply the same serializer to every route that returns User data, including lists, nested populates, search, and error or debug output, so access rules are consistent across routes. Add a regression test that asserts the exact set of keys returned for each role and fails if a new field appears.
